extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers interested in manners, social conduct, and Emersonian essays
extracted.subtask_description: An essayistic treatment of manners and behavior that lays out what constitutes good conduct, how manners function socially, and examples/anti-patterns. It offers evaluative claims about the qualities and origins of 'good manners.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners are about 'how', not 'what'
rubrics_metrics.description: Manners: not _what_, but _how_. Life expresses. A statue has no tongue, and needs none. Good tableaux do not need declamation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manners are the form and manner in which actions are done; the proper manner enhances the action itself. Evaluation: focus on execution (gesture, attitude, carriage) rather than merely the content of speech or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners as felicitous or 'happy' ways of doing things
rubrics_metrics.description: Manners are the happy ways of doing things; each once a stroke of genius or of love,--now repeated and hardened into usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good manners are elegant, appropriate, and refined routines that arise from insight or care and become socially repeated practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners are communicable and teachable
rubrics_metrics.description: Manners are very communicable: men catch them from each other. Consuelo... boasted of the lessons she had given the nobles in manners; Talma taught Napoleon the arts of behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One acquires manners by close contact, instruction, and imitation; social environments and schooling are legitimate means to cultivate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners confer social acceptance independent of other merits
rubrics_metrics.description: There are certain manners which... if a person have them, he or she must be considered, and is everywhere welcome, though without beauty, or wealth, or genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing social suitability, manners can outweigh wealth, beauty, or talent; politeness functions as a social passport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners as the minor morals / basics of civility
rubrics_metrics.description: Their first service is very low,--when they are the minor morals; but 'tis the beginning of civility,--to make us, I mean, endurable to each other. ... compel them to be clean; overawe their spite and meanness, teach them to stifle the base, and choose the generous expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate manners by their capacity to make social life tolerable: cleanliness, restraint of base impulses, and polite forms count as foundational moral practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid specific social anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad behavior the laws cannot reach. ... the contradictors and railers at public and private tables ... the overbold, who make their own invitation to your hearth; the persevering talker ... the pitiers of themselves ... the frivolous ... the monotones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These behaviors are socially injurious; a judgment of manners should flag such anti-patterns (interrupting, excessive self-pity, monopolizing conversation, coarse rudeness, monotonous or exhausting presence) as failures of good behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local/institutional rules are pragmatic manners
rubrics_metrics.description: In the hotels on the banks of the Mississippi, they print... 'No gentleman can be permitted to come to the public table without his coat;' ... placards plead with the worshipper against the fury of expectoration. ... cautions ... not to speak loud; ... not to handle engravings; ... not smite statues with canes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical house rules express concrete expectations of decorum; evaluation should attend to such explicit local conventions as measures of appropriate conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners grow from circumstances and character
rubrics_metrics.description: Manners are factitious, and grow out of circumstances as well as out of character. ... Broad lands and great interests not only arrive to such heads as can manage them, but form manners of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging manners, consider both learned/adopted behaviors and those rooted in upbringing, position, or temperament; manners often reflect social station and environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for culture (heritage) shapes manners
rubrics_metrics.description: Manners are partly factitious, but, mainly, there must be capacity for culture in the blood. Else all culture is vain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay asserts that innate or inherited capacity for refinement influences the depth of manners; evaluations invoking improvement should account for natural aptitude as a limiting/enabling factor (descriptive, not prescriptive).

rubrics_metrics.name: The body (eyes, face, gait, posture) is the primary vehicle of manners
rubrics_metrics.description: The soul which animates nature is ... published in the figure, movement, and gesture of animated bodies. ... The visible carriage or action of the individual, as resulting from his organization and his will combined, we call manners. ... The face and eyes reveal what the spirit is doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess manners by observing bodily expression — eye behavior, bearing, walk, voice and gesture — because these reveal character more truly than words; pay particular attention to congruence between outward carriage and inner intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eyes over tongue: ocular truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: When the eyes say one thing, and the tongue another, a practised man relies on the language of the first. ... The eyes of men converse as much as their tongues, with the advantage, that the ocular dialect needs no dictionary, but is understood all the world over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give greater weight to eye contact and ocular expression than to spoken disclaimers when judging sincerity or the quality of manners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtly/civil service manners: calm bearing and polished speech
rubrics_metrics.description: A calm and resolute bearing, a polished speech, an embellishment of trifles, and the art of hiding all uncomfortable feeling, are essential to the courtier: ... it is a point of pride with kings to remember faces and names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In formal/palatial settings evaluate bearing for composure, memory for names/faces, urbane speech, and the skill of masking personal discomfort to preserve decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reliance and self-possession as foundation of good manners
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis of good manners is self-reliance. Necessity is the law of all who are not self-possessed. Those who are not self-possessed, obtrude, and pain us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure manners by the individual's inner poise: confidence that neither obtrudes nor apologizes; self-possession enables generous, natural comportment rather than anxious or servile behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners require time; haste is vulgar
rubrics_metrics.description: Manners require time, as nothing is more vulgar than haste. Friendship should be surrounded with ceremonies and respects, and not crushed into corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patience, leisure, and ceremonial attention are marks of good manners; evaluate social interaction for appropriate pacing and respectfulness rather than hurried brusqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity over mere effect; what is done for effect is seen
rubrics_metrics.description: What is done for effect, is seen to be done for effect; what is done for love, is felt to be done for love. A man inspires affection and honor, because he was not lying in wait for these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether manners are genuine expressions of character rather than performed artifices; insincerity is detectable and reduces the value of outward civility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manners as social instrument/power (strategic courtesy)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the talent of that character so common,--the successful man of the world,--in all marts, senates, and drawing-rooms? Manners: mariners of power; sense to see his advantage, and manners up to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that manners can be used instrumentally to gain influence; critique should note when courtesy is tactical versus when it springs from genuine regard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novels and conversation as tests/records of manners and mutual understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Novels are the journal or record of manners; ... the best of life is conversation, and the greatest success is confidence, or perfect understanding between sincere people. 'rien que s'entendre', good understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cultural artifacts (novels, conversations) for their portrayal of manners and for their capacity to convey sincere mutual understanding; value sincere rapport as the pinnacle of social success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical features (nose, teeth, gait) express character and are readable
rubrics_metrics.description: The sculptor, ... will tell you how significant a feature is the nose; how its forms express strength or weakness of will, and good or bad temper. The nose of Julius Caesar, of Dante, and of Pitt, suggest 'the terrors of the beak.' What refinement, and what limitations, the teeth betray!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay suggests readers naturally infer character from physical features; when assessing a person's manners, note how bodily particulars (walk, nose, teeth, carriage) contribute to perceived character — though be cautious about undue determinism.
